A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoIN/AIUTA research. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite the revised title and evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation benchmarks, a human study, component ablations and IDKVQA uncertainty-estimation experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports revised navigation and human-study results, retained ablations and IDKVQA experiments, plus original runtime, distractor-success and question-diversity analyses.

M1.justification: The reasoning LLM changes from Llama 3.1 70B to GPT-4o in Section 6. This substitutes a model component, while the VLFM/LLaVA pipeline, Self-Questioner, Interaction Trigger, prompts and Algorithms 1–3 remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 removes evaluation with freely composed, detailed initial instructions, retaining category-only initialization in the human study. The indoor navigation and IDKVQA coverage otherwise remains substantially the same; the enlarged validation splits primarily change sample counts.

E2.justification: OVON, cited but not evaluated in v1, joins the navigation comparison in v2 Table 2. Monolithic, PSL and VLFM remain, as do the MaxProb, LP and Energy Score comparators on IDKVQA.

E3.justification: Seen/synonym/unseen validation splits expand from 82/36/47 to 831/359/459 episodes. Main comparisons omit Train, while the corresponding component ablation is retained as the Ablation split. The human study changes from 15 participants and 16 episodes under two input conditions to 20 participants and 40 category-only episodes. v2 also changes the LLM and introduces Distractor Success and runtime-profiling protocols.

E4.justification: The original component ablation, uncertainty comparison and threshold-sensitivity analysis remain. Supplementary Sections D, F and G add three distinct investigations: runtime profiling over 20 episodes, diagnosis of VLFM stopping at distractors, and question-diversity analysis using 414 questions and UMAP.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 first reports means and standard deviations for distractor counts and path lengths, describing dataset variability. The repeated-subset sensitivity analysis is retained. Neither version specifies navigation confidence intervals or a statistical test supporting the human-versus-simulation comparison.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and human-study results are replaced under revised settings. AIUTA's seen/synonym/unseen SR changes from 8.64/11.11/12.77 to 7.42/14.38/6.67; these are not same-setting performance changes. OVON, distractor-success and runtime results are added, while component-ablation and IDKVQA scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The target-fact update, entropy formulation, certainty-threshold rule and Effective Reliability formulas remain unchanged. No theorem, proof, derivation or substantive formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The CoIN, AIUTA, CoIN-Bench and IDKVQA contributions remain. v2 recasts AIUTA as a competitive, policy-independent baseline and emphasizes unseen-category generalization and simulated-user validity, replacing v1's explicit empirical claim about flexibility with detailed initial requests.

C2.justification: Interpretation shifts from arbitrary-input flexibility and VLM response errors toward trained-policy generalization failures and validation of simulated users. v2 adds distractor-based failure explanations and identifies LLM calls as the runtime bottleneck. It removes the explicit cloud/privacy caveat and asserts no statistical differences in the human comparison without specifying a test.

D1.justification: v2 adds OVON implementation details, NVIDIA 4090 runtime measurements, optimization disclosures, question-embedding information and a conditional code/benchmark release statement. Prompts and pseudocode are retained. The earlier human-study episode IDs and explicit IDKVQA non-overlap assurance are removed; this does not establish that overlap was introduced.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted comparisons with personalized instance navigation and ChatGPT Asks, BLIP-2 Answers, clarifying differences from prior VLM–LLM captioning dialogues. References also change with GPT-4o and the new analyses, including removal of the Llama 3 citation. The broader navigation, interaction and uncertainty positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, benchmark description, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The supplement is reorganized from Sections A–E to A–J, separating the human study and inserting explanatory and analytical sections. Method descriptions and prompts remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main comparison table adds OVON and removes Train columns; the human-study table removes the input column and detailed-instruction rows. v2 adds dataset statistics, distance histograms, an evaluation diagram, a distractor-success table and a question UMAP. Category plots are redrawn and displays relocated, while core schematics and example images are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded validation comparison with OVON and new runtime and failure analyses strengthen the empirical assessment. The gain is limited by removed episode-level reproducibility details and new reporting problems: Section 6's fold improvements do not follow Table 2, and the claimed absence of statistical differences between human and simulated users has no specified test.
